hook: [focused] Eighty-four thousandths of a second. [surprised] Less than the blink of an eye. [ironic] Enough to lose pole position… at home.
laps: Melbourne, twenty twenty-five. Home race for Oscar Piastri, born right here. Standing in the way: not a rival. A teammate.
sectors: Norris takes sector one. Piastri, sector two. Norris, sector three. The start and the finish: in Formula One, those are the only ones anyone remembers.

T1: Turn 1. Look at the apex. Norris in fifth, Piastri in fourth. One gear down, nine kilometres an hour down.
And the exit confirms the verdict.
Nine hundredths, gone at the very first corner.
T6: Turn 6. Piastri strikes back. Look at the dotted lines: Piastri brakes twenty metres later. Twenty metres of pure nerve.
Seven kilometres an hour more at the apex.
Four hundredths of a second, clawed back.
T10: Turn 10. Same nerve, same reward. Ten kilometres an hour more on the way in…
… and five more hundredths in the bank. The local hero is fighting back.
T13: Then comes turn 13. The final judge. Norris gets out faster…
… and takes back ten hundredths in one go. Everything Piastri won on the brakes, Norris takes back on the exit.

summary: So. Piastri wins where it takes courage. Norris wins where it takes patience. And that day, patience wins by eighty-four thousandths of a second.
topSpeed: On the straights, nothing to choose: three twenty-nine against three twenty-eight. The difference isn't in the engine. It's in the corners.

epilogue.title: In the rain, Norris wins · Piastri 9th
epilogue.voice: The next day, the rain arrives. Norris wins. Piastri, running second, goes off at turn 12 and finishes ninth. At home.

end: Every session's telemetry: metrikdelta dot com.
